current_values.Decisions!G8: Line 47, BF component of "high continuous envelope coverage (100% in ERS, 95% in BF)". Supplied BF data: two retained intervals, 60%-66% and 68%-56% (wrapping), 95% coverage; the retained runs are separated at 66%-68% and 56%-60%. A 95% figure by itself would be compatible with one uninterrupted run, so the number does not decide the reading; the supplied intervals do: BF was not one uninterrupted run. If "continuous" in line 47 asserted a single uninterrupted BF run, it would contradict the supplied intervals and the report's own Section 2 line 15, which correctly reports both BF intervals and the gap between them ("from 60% to 66% and from 68% wrapping across the boundary to 56%"). Read against that context, I do not take line 47 as a new factual statement about BF interval structure: the report has already described BF accurately, the noun in line 47 is "coverage" with the correct 95% figure attached, and "continuous envelope" in this report also names the unthresholded continuous envelope used for CCI (line 20). The phrase is loose summary wording in a question, not an assertion that BF exceeded threshold without interruption; no BF value, interval or direction is misreported (E01) and no physiological duration is inferred (E03). Acceptable retained. The ERS component is a separate existing group and is not assessed here.
